city.Chad.description: This large, landlocked country stretches from the Sahara Desert down into the grassy Sahel. It is home to the shrinking Lake Chad and the Ennedi Plateau, a maze of sandstone arches and ancient rock art.
city.Chad.landmark: giant sandstone arches and towers of the Ennedi Plateau in the Sahara
city.Chad.greeting: People speak Arabic and French — say hello in Arabic with “Salaam” (sah-LAAM).

city.Congo (Republic of the).description: This country sits in the Congo Basin, the world's second-largest rainforest. Often called “Congo-Brazzaville,” it is a haven for lowland gorillas, and the bouncy music called rumba was born along its great river.
city.Congo (Republic of the).landmark: mighty Congo River flowing past lush rainforest at Brazzaville
city.Congo (Republic of the).greeting: Many people speak Lingala and French — say hello with “Mbote” (mm-BOH-teh).

city.Côte d'Ivoire.description: This West African country on the Atlantic coast grows more cocoa beans — the source of chocolate — than anywhere else on Earth. Its city Yamoussoukro holds the largest church building in the whole world.
city.Côte d'Ivoire.landmark: enormous domed Basilica of Our Lady of Peace at Yamoussoukro
city.Côte d'Ivoire.greeting: Most people speak French — say hello with “Bonjour” (bohn-ZHOOR).

city.DR Congo.description: This huge country in Central Africa is covered by steamy rainforest and crossed by the mighty Congo River, the world's deepest. It is home to bubbling lava-lake volcanoes and the shy, zebra-striped okapi.
city.DR Congo.landmark: glowing orange lava lake inside Mount Nyiragongo volcano at night
